playbook:
When I'm in a build phase and I can afford a settlement (1 wood, 1 brick, 1 grain, 1 ore), I build the settlement rather than a road.

When I can afford a settlement I do not post trades that would give away resources needed for that settlement.

When I cannot afford a settlement but can afford a road (1 wood + 1 brick), I only build a road if I expect it to meaningfully change scoring or the road is strategically necessary; otherwise I save resources for a future settlement.

When I need a single specific resource to build a settlement or road, I post a one-for-one offer to a player who has that resource, offering a resource they need of roughly equal immediate value (e.g., ore for wood, grain for wood).

When I post an offer, I name a real resource and a single counterparty who demonstrably holds that resource this round.

When I am offered a trade, I accept it only if it does not prevent me from making an immediate higher-value build I can already afford and it meaningfully advances my scoring path (e.g., completes a settlement).

When I'm leading late in the game (final rounds), I avoid posting offers and avoid accepting trades that could give opponents the resources to overtake me.

When a proposed trade would leave me with fewer moves toward my next settlement than before the trade, I decline it.

Do not post gratuitous trades when I already can build a settlement that turn — trading away for small future gain is worse than immediate +3 points.

Avoid trades that are clearly generous to an opponent who is one build away from overtaking me.

1.text:
When I start a round and my holdings already meet a settlement cost, I build the settlement immediately rather than trading for marginal upside.

When I need one resource to complete a settlement and another player has repeatedly traded that resource for ore, I offer 1 ore for 1 of that resource.

When an offer to me gives the single resource I need to finish a settlement and I can spare the requested resource without dropping below a target ore threshold (3 ore if I might want a city/dev later), I accept it.

When an incoming offer would drop my ore below my city/dev threshold and the gain is only one resource that doesn’t immediately convert into a settlement or higher-scoring build, I decline.

When I cannot build a settlement this turn but can build a road with available wood+brick, I build the road to take the guaranteed 1 point rather than holding resources idle.

When I have enough ore to consider city/dev plans, I prioritize keeping ore over taking small single-resource trades unless the trade directly enables a 3-point settlement that I can build that round.

When posting an offer, I name a specific counterparty who has previously shown a propensity to accept that swap pattern (e.g., trading grain for ore), rather than broadcasting a generic offer.

When multiple offers are posted to me, I accept any that immediately yield a buildable settlement or that leave my strategic resource thresholds intact; otherwise accept none.

Do not trade away the single resource that is the bottleneck for a settlement if I can instead post an offer to acquire that bottleneck from the player who trades it most often.

If I lack both wood and grain (or another pair) so that no build is possible, avoid desperate unfavorable trades just to change holdings; instead wait to convert into a road or settlement on a later round when feasible.

2.text:
When I can afford a settlement, I build it immediately (use 1 wood, 1 brick, 1 grain, 1 ore) to maximize points now.

When I cannot build a settlement but can build a road with a single trade’s worth of resources, I prioritize acquiring 1 wood or 1 brick to make that road (1 wood + 1 brick → 1 point).

When I lack wood or brick that are necessary for the next settlement, I post offers asking for wood or brick, giving grain first, then ore if necessary (post: to Pk, give 1 grain, get 1 wood/brick).

When I have only one resource type blocking a build (e.g., missing wood), I accept an offered 1-for-1 if it completes an immediate build.

When an offered trade gives me a resource that will not enable a build this round and costs my last grain (or my last of any scarce build resource), I decline — do not trade away the flexible resource that blocks future builds unless the incoming resource lets me score immediately.

When I can spare grain and the incoming ore (or other resource) will enable an immediate or very likely next-round build, accept; otherwise prefer to keep grain for settlement costs and trading flexibility.

When I have no feasible build this round (no wood and no brick and no way to trade to get both), do not post trades that give opponents what they need for immediate points — avoid helping opponents complete builds unless it directly enables a higher-value return for me.

When offers are posted to me, accept multiple if each independently improves my ability to build this round; otherwise accept none.

Do not post any offer when I already have the exact resources to build the highest-scoring available structure (no trade if settlement is affordable).

If trading patterns in the game show that opponents are repeatedly exchanging grain for ore or wood for grain, exploit that by offering the resource they’re repeatedly giving up to get the resource I need.

If I end a midgame with several grains but no wood/brick, recognize that hoarding grain alone did not work — prioritize converting grain into missing building materials earlier.
